overview.summary: A collapse vector showing how every obvious corrective action was delayed because the culture assumed the window would reopen later.
overview.thesis: Deferral became a budget strategy, then a civilizational identity, then a death schedule.
overview.viewer_hint: The timeline page is the best way to watch 'later' harden into policy.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.body: The simulator repeats the same answer across decades. Storage will come later. Retreat will come later. Rationing will come later. The archive marks the repetition as the real model output, not as a rhetorical flourish.

sections.title: Policy behavior
sections.body: Each new impact justified waiting because previous delays had already raised the cost of acting. Leaders kept choosing the option that preserved present legitimacy at the expense of any future that still required legitimacy to arrive.

sections.title: Recovered excerpt
sections.body: Resource temporarily unavailable. Storage later. Retreat later. Rationing later. The language remained procedural enough to pass as planning, even after planning had become a way to postpone admitting that the window was gone.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.body: Unlike overt denial systems, this model captures cultures that accept the danger and still refuse the cost of behaving as if danger is true. The archive treats that gap as one of the most common collapse vectors it sees.

events.label: First adaptation package
events.body: Municipal planners propose staged retreat and storage buildout.

events.label: Budget deferment
events.body: Visible risks are acknowledged but hard costs are postponed to preserve political stability.

events.label: Serial emergency
events.body: Repeated shocks make every corrective option more expensive and therefore easier to delay again.

events.label: Window closure
events.body: The archive marks the system as locked into permanent later.
